advisory.finding: The documented bare-list input branch of _load_jobs() is untested. The docstring and module docstring both state the loader accepts 'a bare list of jobs' (scripts/summarize_ci_failures.py:27,148), and line 154 handles it via `return list(payload)`, but every test feeds either the {"jobs": [...]} dict shape or empty input — no test passes a top-level JSON array. coaching.subject: CLI entrypoint timeout-detection wiring

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `--paginate` to the check-runs annotations fetch so a timeout annotation beyond the first page is not missed (which would mislabel a TIMED OUT job as CANCELLED).
evidence: 407: jobs_json="$(gh api --paginate \  (jobs fetch DOES paginate; annotations fetch does not)
dropped.finding: The per-job check-run annotations fetch (`gh api repos/.../check-runs/${job_id}/annotations`) is not paginated, unlike the jobs fetch which uses `--paginate`. A timed-out job whose timeout annotation is not on the first page (annotations default to 30 per page) would be reported as CANCELLED rather than TIMED OUT — defeating the exact timeout-vs-cancel distinction this change exists to provide.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard `_is_timeout`/`describe_job` against an annotations value that is not a list of dicts, so a malformed ANNOTATIONS_JSON degrades wording rather than raising.
evidence: 92:         TIMEOUT_MARKER in str(annotation.get("message", "")).lower() for annotation in annotations
130:     annotations = annotations or {}  (no per-value type check that it is a list of dicts)
dropped.finding: `_is_timeout` assumes every annotations value is a list of dicts and calls `annotation.get("message", "")` per element. If ANNOTATIONS_JSON maps a job id to a non-list (e.g. a dict such as a GitHub error object `{"message": ...}`), iterating yields dict keys (strings) and `.get` raises AttributeError, aborting the whole summary. The workflow guards HTTP failures with `|| echo '[]'`, but the module itself is not defensive against a malformed map.
dropped.suggested_fix: In `_is_timeout`, coerce/guard: `for annotation in annotations if isinstance(annotation, dict)`, and in `summarize` ensure `annotations.get(...)` yields a list before use.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Document (or defensively verify) the 'Actions job id == check-run id' assumption that timeout detection depends on, since a silent divergence mislabels every timeout as a cancellation.
evidence: 413: # for the non-successful jobs only. A job id IS its check-run id. Best-effort: a
dropped.finding: Timeout detection relies on the unstated assumption that the Actions job `id` equals its check-run `id` (comment: 'A job id IS its check-run id'). This is empirically true for GitHub Actions today but is an undocumented external API coupling; if it ever diverges, every timed-out job silently regresses to being labeled CANCELLED with no failing signal (the annotation fetch just 404s into `[]`).

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an entrypoint test that passes a non-empty ANNOTATIONS_JSON with a timeout marker for a `cancelled` job and asserts 'TIMED OUT' in stdout.
evidence: scripts/summarize_ci_failures.py:161: `    job_annotations = json.loads(raw_annotations) if raw_annotations else {}`
tests/scripts/test_summarize_ci_failures.py:201-212: `_run` default `annotations_json: str = ""`; all three entrypoint tests omit it
Entrypoint tests assert only on a `failure` job, a green run, and empty input — none asserts a `cancelled` job + timeout annotation yields TIMED OUT via the CLI
dropped.finding: The CLI entrypoint's timeout-detection wiring is never exercised. The load-bearing distinction (a `cancelled` conclusion promoted to TIMED OUT via the annotation) is only tested against the in-process summarize() seam; all three subprocess tests (_run) pass an empty ANNOTATIONS_JSON, so the entrypoint's `json.loads(raw_annotations)` branch (line 161) that plumbs annotations into summarize() is never run. A break in the entrypoint's annotation parsing/plumbing would produce a byte-identical CANCELLED-vs-TIMED-OUT collapse — the exact bug this change exists to fix — with no failing test.
dropped.suggested_fix: Add `test_entrypoint_distinguishes_timeout_via_annotations` calling `_run('{"jobs":[{"id":1,"name":"slow","conclusion":"cancelled"}]}', '{"1":[{"message":"The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 30m0s"}]}')` and asserting 'TIMED OUT' in `result.stdout`.
